examples: Aim 1 will test whether a peer-led self-management program delivered by telephone and video reduces fatigue and pain interference in rural adults with chronic illness.
Aim 2 will find the barriers that keep rural adults with multiple chronic conditions from specialty care and from self-management support.
Aim 3 will adapt a symptom self-monitoring diary with patient-reported outcomes for people with energy-limiting chronic illness and pilot test its feasibility and acceptability.
Aim 4 will evaluate whether training peer facilitators as community health workers improves engagement and retention in a behavioral intervention.
profile.expertise: Ten years of peer support groups for adults who live with chronic illness. Ran 2 member surveys on fatigue, pain, and access to care. The team includes a program director with a public health degree, a part-time research lead with a doctorate in health services research, and 22 trained peer facilitators.
profile.research_summary: We study how adults who live with chronic illness manage fatigue, chronic pain, and gaps in access to care in rural communities. We work as a community organization with trained peer facilitators, member surveys, and community-based participatory methods, so that self-management support reaches people who live far from specialty clinics.
profile.resources: A member list of 1,400 adults with chronic illness in 14 rural counties. A 2025 member survey with 412 responses. A telephone and video meeting system that the support groups already use. A written agreement with a university partner for human subjects review.
